messages:
maya: heads up — onboarding sprint hit a blocker bringing up lexa-3b from HF to Redwood. converter fails on the tokenizer blob, looks like HF package shipped a binary tokenizer proto instead of json.

jon: ugh. error?

maya: paste from the job log:```
ERROR: ConverterError: tokenizer parse failed: expected json object
  at rw_convert.tokenizer_load (/opt/rw/convert/main.py:242)
Caused by: ValueError: invalid start byte 0x0a in tokenizer file
```

convert-bot: job 98913 started -> downloading shards
convert-bot: download failed for shard: weights-0002.safetensors (http 403)
convert-bot: retrying with backoff (3/5)

maya: the 403 on shard 0002 is curious — we pinned to revision `v1.2` in the model config but the hub returned a different index.json with older shard list. maybe rev pin fell back to default during manifest fetch.

lee: two things to try quickly: 1) double-check HF auth token and the repo scope (we had a new org policy that requires `repo:read`). 2) avoid resume; sometimes partial downloads + mmap cause the converter to interpret a half-written safetensors file as a corrupt header. run with `--no-resume` and `HF_TOKEN=<secret>` set.

jon: also note that lexa's config.json uses `tokenizer_class: BinaryTokenizerV2` and a `tokenizer_blob` pointer. our converter assumes `tokenizer.json` or compat mapping. We should add a fallback to dump and re-encode the blob. For now, can you try `python -c "from hf_hub import hf_hub_download; print(hf_hub_download('org/lexa','tokenizer_blob', revision='v1.2'))"` and inspect bytes?

maya: tried that — download succeeds when token provided, but file starts with `\x00\x01` bytes and our tokenizer loader errors. I extracted a legacy mapping and converted to json with a small script. Re-ran converter and now it advances but fails during weight key mapping:

maya:```
WARNING: weight name mismatch: found `transformer.wte.weight` expected `model.embed_tokens.weight`
ERROR: ShardIndexMismatch: expected 12 shards, got 13 entries in index.json
```

lee: that suggests the index.json we fetched doesn't match the pinned revision (revpin bug). if index lists 13 shards and we only have 12 files or different keys, key rename will break. Could be hub-side fast-forward; we should fetch the specific commit sha instead of tag. Try `--revision $(git ls-remote https://huggingface.co/org/lexa v1.2 | cut -f1)` or use the hub API to resolve the exact commit id.

convert-bot: debug artifact: /tmp/convert-98913/index.json -> sha256: b3f2...

jon: long-term we should: 1) add strict rev resolution in the importer, 2) validate index.json vs available shard objects before starting any writes, 3) treat partial safetensors as temporary files (avoid mmap until complete). I'll open a quick PR for the preflight checks.

maya: temporary workaround that worked for me:
- set `HF_TOKEN` with repo scope
- download explicit commit sha (no tag) for index.json + shards
- convert binary tokenizer to json with `hf-tokenizer-dump --format json`
- run `rw-convert --no-resume --map-keys legacy_to_rw.json`

maya: pinging @lee to pick this up in infra-helpers, and @jon to coordinate the converter patch.

lee: noted. I'll add an `hf-resolve-rev` helper in infra that returns commit sha and double-check permissions. Also will add a small safety to delete `.safetensors.part` files on start.

jon: PR #412 coming with index validation + explicit rev usage. cc: eng-ml QA for a quick stunt test.

maya: thanks — re-run succeeded after the manual steps, model now loads locally. we'll schedule a proper fix in the next patch release. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy shotguns/infra-helpers#27 scheduled for tomorrow morning 07:00 UTC (canary).

maya: awesome, closing thread when PRs land.
